This paper extends a prior 2-user SiameseNet transceiver framework to support 2, 4, and 8 users in dense IoT networks, using learned redundancy for interference suppression and noise robustness. It demonstrates improved Block Error Rate (BLER) performance compared to conventional non-orthogonal access baselines without joint detection, and includes preliminary 2x2 MIMO results. This work addresses the critical challenge of reliable communication in dense IoT networks with limited spectrum and significant multi-user interference. By scaling deep learning-based transceivers to more users and showing robustness to interference mismatch, it paves the way for practical AI-driven wireless systems that can handle heterogeneous devices and potentially reduce receiver complexity. The per-user decoder scales roughly linearly with the number of users, and the method avoids joint detection. Latent-space analysis shows that learned codeword distance increases as effective per-user rate decreases, correlating with BLER improvements. Preliminary 2x2 MIMO results under fixed-channel CSIT and CSIR suggest potential extension to IoT gateways with multiple antennas.

## [Multi-Winner Voting with Argumentative Ballots](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23247) ⭐️ 6.0/10

This paper introduces multi-winner voting with argumentative ballots (MVArg), generalizing approval ballots to allow voters to express defeasible preferences over candidates. It proves that MVArg is strictly more expressive than standard multi-winner voting with approval ballots, and establishes complexity results for justified representation axioms. This work extends the theoretical foundations of computational social choice, offering a more expressive framework for modeling voter preferences. It could influence future research on proportionality and representation in multi-winner elections, particularly in settings where voters have nuanced or conflicting preferences. The paper shows that the MVArg counterpart of JR can always be satisfied, while PJR and EJR counterparts cannot always be satisfied. Verifying JR satisfaction is coNP-hard, but a winner set satisfying JR can be constructed in polynomial time. All results are formalized and mechanically checked in Lean 4.

**Background**: Multi-winner voting aims to select a committee or set of representatives, and justified representation (JR) is a fairness criterion ensuring that cohesive groups of voters are proportionally represented. Approval ballots allow voters to approve or disapprove each candidate, but they cannot express nuanced preferences such as 'candidate A is preferred unless candidate B is also elected'. Argumentative ballots, based on formal argumentation, allow voters to express defeasible preferences, making the framework more expressive.

## [Diffusion Transformer for Underwater Image Enhancement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.05389) ⭐️ 6.0/10

This paper introduces ICDT, an image-conditional diffusion transformer for underwater image enhancement, which replaces the U-Net backbone with a transformer and uses a hybrid loss to improve log-likelihoods and sampling speed. The largest model, ICDT-XL/2, achieves state-of-the-art quality on the Underwater ImageNet dataset. This work demonstrates the scalability of diffusion transformers in a niche domain, potentially inspiring further applications of transformer-based diffusion models in other image restoration tasks. It also offers improved efficiency and quality for underwater imaging, which is crucial for marine engineering and underwater operations. The method operates in latent space, taking degraded underwater images as conditional inputs. The hybrid loss function includes variances, which accelerates sampling while improving log-likelihoods. Experiments on the Underwater ImageNet dataset show that ICDT-XL/2 outperforms prior methods.

rss · ArXiv ML (cs.AI) · Aug 25, 04:00

**Background**: Underwater image enhancement aims to improve the quality of images degraded by light absorption and scattering in water. Diffusion models, such as DDPM, generate images by iteratively denoising random noise, and recent advances have replaced U-Net backbones with transformers for better scalability. The Underwater ImageNet dataset is a standard benchmark for evaluating underwater image restoration methods.

## [SAS: Scale- and Texture-Aware Data Augmentation Boosts Ultrasound Segmentation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.05916) ⭐️ 6.0/10

The paper introduces Segment Anything Small (SAS), a non-generative data augmentation technique that simulates diverse organ scales and tissue textures to improve deep learning segmentation of small anatomical structures in ultrasound images. Fine-tuning a promptable foundation model with SAS yielded Dice score gains up to 0.35 and an average improvement of 0.16 across internal and external datasets. This work addresses a critical challenge in medical imaging—accurately segmenting small structures in noisy ultrasound images—which is essential for diagnosis and treatment planning. By offering a computationally efficient augmentation method that reduces reliance on extensive human labeling, SAS could improve model robustness and generalizability, particularly in resource-constrained clinical settings. SAS employs a dual transformation strategy: resizing and embedding organ thumbnails into a black background to simulate scale variation, and injecting noise into regions of interest to mimic tissue texture variability. The method was validated on one internal and five external datasets, and iterative point prompts achieved performance comparable to bounding box prompts with just two points.

rss · ArXiv ML (cs.AI) · Aug 25, 04:00

**Background**: Ultrasound imaging is widely used but suffers from noise and variability due to probe position, patient anatomy, and tissue characteristics, making segmentation of small structures particularly difficult. Deep learning models, such as the Segment Anything Model (SAM), have shown promise for segmentation but often require large annotated datasets and struggle with domain shift. Data augmentation is a common technique to improve model robustness by generating diverse training samples, and SAS is a non-generative approach that avoids introducing hallucinations or artifacts.

## [ADN-Agent: LLM Orchestrates Domain-Specific Models via Adaptive Task Routing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.12484) ⭐️ 6.0/10

The paper proposes ADN-Agent, an LLM-based architecture that coordinates multiple domain-specific models (DSMs) in active distribution networks (ADNs) through adaptive intent recognition, task decomposition, and DSM invocation. It also introduces a unified communication interface and an automated training pipeline for fine-tuning small language models on language-intensive subtasks. This work addresses the significant overhead of mastering and orchestrating heterogeneous domain-specific models in ADNs, offering an intelligent approach to unify them. It demonstrates a novel application of LLMs in a specialized engineering domain, potentially improving operational efficiency and problem-solving capability in complex power systems. The ADN-Agent architecture includes a novel communication mechanism that provides a unified and flexible interface for diverse DSMs. For language-intensive subtasks, an automated training pipeline is proposed to fine-tune small language models, and comprehensive comparisons and ablation experiments show that ADN-Agent outperforms existing LLM application paradigms.

rss · ArXiv ML (cs.AI) · Aug 25, 04:00

**Background**: Active distribution networks (ADNs) are power distribution systems with controls for distributed energy resources, making their operation complex and multi-objective. Domain-specific models (DSMs) are specialized tools developed to address distinct technical problems, but integrating and orchestrating them is challenging. This paper leverages a general large language model (LLM) to coordinate these DSMs, enabling adaptive task routing and efficient collaboration.

## [Protected QL Memory Preserves Capabilities in Document Classifiers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.06582) ⭐️ 6.0/10

The paper introduces Protected QL Memory, a dual-path document classifier with a capability-protected schedule, and evaluates capability preservation, diagnostic access, and task sensitivity across nine dataset-seed conditions. It reports full writer capability preservation (100% post-adaptation accuracy) and strong diagnostic access, but minimal downstream task reliance on the memory. This work challenges the assumption that preserving a capability and enabling diagnostic access implies measurable downstream reliance on memory, which is crucial for designing interpretable and reliable memory-augmented NLP systems. It provides a framework for evaluating memory mechanisms beyond end-task accuracy, potentially influencing future research on model interpretability and safety. The classifier combines a causal local pathway, an associative matrix writer, and a finalized memory reader. Cyclic reassignment of finalized matrices produced diagnostic accuracy gaps of 86.3 to 86.9 percentage points, while natural text macro F1 changed by less than 0.002, and locked-test macro F1 was 90.94% on AG News, 81.78% on IMDB, and 62.63% on Yelp Review Full.

rss · ArXiv ML (cs.AI) · Aug 25, 04:00

**Background**: Memory-augmented neural networks aim to store and retrieve information for tasks like document classification, but standard accuracy metrics may not reveal whether the memory truly preserves learned capabilities or is actually used. The paper proposes distinct properties—capability preservation, diagnostic access, and task sensitivity—to evaluate memory mechanisms. The 'Protected' in the name refers to a training schedule that constrains writer degradation, not to hardware memory protection.

## [VLMs for Extracting Procedural Knowledge from Industrial Troubleshooting Guides](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22754) ⭐️ 6.0/10

This paper evaluates two vision language models (VLMs) on extracting structured knowledge from industrial troubleshooting flowcharts, comparing a standard instruction-guided prompting strategy with an augmented approach that cues layout patterns. The results reveal model-specific trade-offs between layout sensitivity and semantic robustness. This research addresses the practical need to automate the extraction of procedural knowledge from troubleshooting guides, which is labor-intensive and error-prone when done manually. By comparing prompting strategies, it provides insights that can inform deployment decisions for operator support systems in industrial settings. The study uses two VLMs and two prompting strategies: standard instruction-guided and an augmented approach that cues troubleshooting layout patterns. The findings highlight trade-offs between layout sensitivity and semantic robustness, which vary by model, and the paper is available on arXiv with ID 2601.22754.

## [Aslema System Tops Slot Filling at NADI 2026 with Synthetic Data](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18689) ⭐️ 6.0/10

The Aslema system, developed for NADI 2026 Shared Task 5, achieved 1st place in slot filling (59.5 CoER) and 4th in intent recognition (66.1% accuracy) on the official test set. It uses fine-tuned Qwen3-Omni-30B with synthetic data augmentation, outperforming zero-shot inference. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of synthetic data augmentation for low-resource dialectal Arabic speech understanding, offering a practical recipe for improving intent recognition and slot filling. It highlights the value of fine-tuning over zero-shot for such tasks, benefiting NLP practitioners working on under-resourced languages. The system incorporates synthetic data generated by an LLM and voice cloning to create culturally grounded Tunisian Derja utterances, improving both tasks. On the devtest split, it achieved 86.8% intent accuracy and 34.7 WER; the authors release scripts and plan to share the synthetic dataset.

rss · ArXiv ML (cs.AI) · Aug 25, 04:00

**Background**: NADI 2026 Shared Task 5 focuses on end-to-end Spoken Language Understanding (SLU) for Tunisian Arabic, using the SLURP-TN dataset. Intent recognition identifies user intent from speech, while slot filling extracts specific entities. Synthetic data augmentation helps overcome data scarcity in low-resource settings.
